component.name: AI Hub
component.summary: OpenAI-compatible gateway over your AI subscriptions

description.p: AI Hub turns the AI subscriptions you already pay for into a single local API endpoint. Sign in once per provider with OAuth, and AI Hub hands you one OpenAI-compatible URL and key that any tool expecting the OpenAI API can use — n8n, opencode, Continue, Aider, or your own scripts.

Everything runs on your machine. The gateway listens on localhost, your credentials stay in your home directory, and no request is routed through a server belonging to anyone else. There are no per-token API keys to manage and no per-token bill to watch.

ul.li: OAuth sign-in for Gemini, Claude, Codex, Kimi and xAI subscriptions
One endpoint covering chat, image generation, speech and video
Optional on-device speech: local transcription and text-to-speech that never leave the machine
One-click configuration of the AI tools already installed on your system
A tray icon showing gateway status, with the endpoint and key a click away

screenshot.caption: Start the gateway and copy the endpoint and key your tools use
Sign in to each subscription once, with as many accounts as you have
Connect the AI tools already installed on this computer in one click
See requests, tokens and the quota left on every subscription
Browse every model your subscriptions can serve, by kind

description.p: AI-Proxy is now AI Hub. The first launch moves your sign-ins, gateway key and settings to the new name; every tool you connected keeps working, and the old command name still runs the new ai-hub command.

ul.li: Connected devices: one computer runs the hub, and your other devices use its endpoint, each with a key of its own that can be revoked at any time
Several accounts per provider, each with its own quota gauge; pause one or prefer another, and requests move between them on their own
The command line tool works on Windows again: the launcher the app installed recorded its paths in a form PowerShell could not use
On Linux the Server screen no longer reports the app's own launcher as a conflicting copy of the command on your PATH

description.p: The ai-proxy command line tool now installs from the app itself, on every platform, and can be removed again the same way. Previously the button copied a command to the clipboard that could not work on Windows or Linux, and on macOS installed a build that rewrote the app's own engine configuration.

The gateway now comes back on its own if a sidecar dies, instead of staying down until the app is restarted. Enabling the Device Harness no longer freezes the window while the desktop portal waits for you to answer its permission dialog.

Linux now ships as a Flatpak, and only as a Flatpak. It installs on every distribution with a desktop, including the ARM machines the old AppImage could never be built for. The AppImage and .deb downloads are withdrawn; the headless command-line tarball is unchanged.

Image and video models work from coding agents: images come back as something an agent can display, and video generation joins the media catalog. When a key, port or model list changes, every configured tool can be re-pointed in one click, and the gateway key can be rotated from the Server screen.
The app checks for updates on every platform, with a setting to install them automatically, and the tray's copy actions no longer fail silently.

The model catalog lists only models a provider has proven it can serve, and the health check reports an honest verdict per provider. Image models return pictures coding agents can show, including over streaming.

ul.li: Local speech-to-text and text-to-speech, free and offline, through the standard audio API
Connect Clients rebuilt, with search, a by-status view and one button to re-point every tool
One-click configuration writes to the right place on Windows, and key setup reaches both zsh and bash

description.p: Provider sign-in no longer hangs after a cancelled attempt, removing a login really removes it, and the Remove and Reset buttons work on macOS. One-click configuration of every client needs only a free account.

ul.li: Support for Buzz, Block's team chat with agents
A model catalog that suggests only what each kind of model can do, and a button to reset the app's data
Updates arrive inside the app from this release on

description.p: Fixes starting the server and configuring clients on Windows, and makes the built-in updater work on every platform. Every build now has to start the gateway and answer a health check before it is published.
Fixes the macOS package: the app's signature is sealed correctly and each architecture carries matching helper programs, so the app starts on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.

JSON mode works: the gateway enforces a JSON response format even where the provider ignores it. Usage is attributed per key, and the gateway can be bound to a chosen address for running it for a team.
